title: Sentinel matrix evaluator and graceful model-proxy switcher
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a robust per-dependency/per-model/per-tenant circuit controller that trips based on a confidence-boundized signal derived from both short-term spike detectors and longer-term SLO drift. When tripped, rather than an instant hard cut, traffic should be routed through a model-proxy path (lighter-weight or cached responses) with gradual rejoin probes and a transparent fallback escrow for higher-quality responses.

Background and motivation:
- Current breaker implementations are threshold-heavy and cause noisy hard failures during transient spikes.
- Incidents in multi-region failovers showed large customer error bursts when model endpoints were abruptly cut without a transparent proxy/fallback.
- We want per-entity (tenant/model/dependency) granularity with an ability to (a) safely shed load, (b) maintain SLOs for high-priority tenants, and (c) enable graceful return-to-normal with rejoin probes.

Goals:
1) Implement a "Sentinel Matrix Evaluator" (SME): evaluates multiple signals (latency quantiles, error rates, queue depth, GPU utilization, and model-specific quality metrics) and produces a trip probability with a confidence bound.
2) Replace binary trips with a "Model-Proxy Switcher": routes a configurable percentage of traffic to proxy paths (cache, n-1 model variant, or stub responses) and escalates if conditions worsen.
3) Provide a fallback escrow stage: when proxy returns are lower-quality, offer an async backfill path that attempts a higher-quality response and attaches it to the request/response lifecycle where feasible.
4) Expose telemetry for threshold tuning and an automated calibration job that adjusts trip windows per-tenant using Bayesian smoothing.

Design overview:
- Inputs to SME: rolling windows at 1s/10s/1m for latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), 5m error rate, request concurrency, KV cache hit ratio, and model-quality drift (BLEU/ROUGE-like or application-specific evals).
- Scoring: each signal maps to a normalized risk score 0..1; SME aggregates scores using a weighted geometric mean to avoid domination by noisy signals. We compute a lower-bound and upper-bound on the aggregate using a Beta-Bernoulli bootstrap that gives us a 95% confidence interval on the risk.
- Trip logic: only trigger tiered shedding when the lower-bound exceeds a soft threshold for T consecutive windows OR the upper-bound exceeds a hard threshold. This prevents flapping on brief anomalies.
- Progressive proxying: 0% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% redirect steps with exponentially-backed hold durations. Each step uses a canary probe circuit to attempt limited direct calls; success reduces the shedding step.
- Rejoin: periodic randomized probes (1% of traffic per minute) attempt real model calls with full context; success increments a rejoin score. If rejoin score > 0.8 for N probes, rollback a step.
- Fallback escrow: when proxy returns are inadequate (quality below threshold), spawn an async high-fidelity request to a reserved capacity pool (if available) and write result to an attachment store; client SDKs/console will be able to poll for finalization. This preserves user experience for high-value requests.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1 (POC): instrument SME prototype as a standalone evaluator service (Rust) consuming existing metrics; expose gRPC and local evaluation API.
- Week 2 (integration): wire model-proxy switcher into the router component with feature flags; default to shadowing (no traffic change) for 48h.
- Week 3 (canary): enable progressive proxying for low-traffic tenants in staging; run calibration job that learns per-tenant priors.
- Week 4 (rollout): expand to 10% production tenants with tight monitoring and kill switch.

Acceptance criteria:
- SME correctly computes risk CI and triggers shedding steps in synthetic spike tests 95% of the time.
- No customer-facing 5xx regression in the first 30m of rollout for canary tenants.
- Rejoin probes complete and re-open paths without human intervention in >= 80% of simulated recoveries.
- Latency/SLO dashboards show reduced severity during controlled spikes vs current breaker baseline (measured across p95/p99 and error rate).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for signal normalization and Bayesian CI calculations.
- Integration tests that simulate GPU saturation and network partitions to validate stepwise proxying.
- Chaos test during staging: transient region outage and gradual recovery to verify rejoin behavior.

Observability and runbook:
- Dashboards: per-tenant SME score heatmap, step-level proxy distribution over time, rejoin success rate, escrow queue length.
- Alerts: (a) step escalation > 30s for >3 tenants, (b) escrow queue growth > 1000 items, (c) rejoin probe failure rate > 50% for 10m.
- Runbook excerpt: if escrow queue grows and reserved capacity is exhausted, immediately throttle background backfills and contact SRE lead. Rollback feature flag to shadowing if repeated false positives detected.

Security and compliance notes:
- Escrow data paths must honor tenant encryption policies (KMS). Implementation will reuse existing KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SME+Design+Draft
- Draft API spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-router/pull/1123
- Staging dashboard (examples): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/sme/proxy-canary

Risks and trade-offs:
- Complexity: SME increases decision surface and operational burden; mitigations: start with a conservative default and enable opt-in per team.
- Latency overhead: proxy switching and escrow introduces async work; ensure that proxy path meets latency SLOs for P0 tenants or exclude them from proxying.
- Cost: escrow/backfill reserved capacity has cost; limit by policy and provide billing visibility.

Next steps:
- Review design with SRE and product to lock thresholds and tenant opt-in criteria (meeting 2026-03-04).
- Build POC and schedule integration with router by 2026-03-08.
